stem.en: A party is a recognised State party in two States. It polled 9% of the valid votes in each and won 6 Lok Sabha seats. Is it a national party?

text.en: Yes, 9% is above every figure in the conditions
No, and it now becomes a registered unrecognised party
No, it stays a State party in those two States
No, as a party can be a State party in only one State

explanation.en: The national routes need four States, about 11 seats, or State recognition in four States. This party has two States, 6 seats and two records. It does not lose its State recognition by failing them.

hints.en: Check the three national routes. Then ask if failing them removes its State recognition.
